L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Baricitinib, which shares the pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine and sulfonamide motifs with the query, has an absolute oral bioavailability of nearly 80% in fasted healthy adults.
Ruxolitinib, a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine JAK inhibitor, is reported as >95% bioavailable in healthy subjects and 74% in a human PBPK parameter table.
Sulfonamide-containing sildenafil and vardenafil have human absolute oral bioavailability values of 41% and 34%, respectively, both well above the F >= 20% threshold.
The lowest relevant human oral bioavailability record among the visible contexts, indacaterol at approximately 24%, still exceeds the F >= 20% threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement is available for the query molecule itself.
No intravenous-reference pharmacokinetic data for the query are provided, so first-pass metabolism and systemic clearance are not directly characterized.
Transfer from structurally related pyrrolopyrimidine/sulfonamide drugs is indirect; formulation, dose, and food effects for the query are unknown.
Solubility and permeability are estimated from physicochemical properties rather than measured experimentally.
content.decision_summary: All visible L1 gold-context records report human oral bioavailability values above 20%, and the most structurally relevant pyrrolopyrimidine/sulfonamide contexts (baricitinib, ruxolitinib, sildenafil, vardenafil) range from 34% to >95%. The query has favorable physicochemical properties for absorption, and no affirmative evidence supports F < 20%. Prediction is high, with moderate confidence because the evidence is transferred from related compounds rather than measured directly for the query.
